papers.title: Effect of Different Titanium Surfaces on Maturation of Murine Bone Marrow-Derived Dendritic Cells.
papers.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) play a pivotal role in the host response to implanted biomaterials. Osseointegration of titanium (Ti) implant is an immunological and inflammatory-driven process. However, the role of DCs in this complex process is largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate the effect of different Ti surfaces on DC maturation, and evaluate its subsequent potential on osteogenic differentiation of preosteoblasts. Murine bone marrow-derived DCs were seeded on Ti disks with different surface treatments, including pretreatment (PT), sandblasted/acid-etched (SLA) and modified SLA (modSLA) surface. Compared with DCs cultured on PT and SLA surfaces, the cells seeded on modSLA surface demonstrated a more round morphology with lower expression of CD86 and MHC-II, the DC maturation markers. Those cells also secreted high levels of anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 and TGF-β. Notably, addition of conditioned medium (CM) from modSLA-induced DCs significantly increased the mRNA expression of Runx2 and ALP as well as ALP activity by murine preosteoblast MC3T3-E1 cells. Our data demonstrated that Ti disks with different surfaces lead to differential DCs responses. PT and SLA surfaces induce DCs mature, while DCs seeded on modSLA-Ti surface maintain an immature phenotype and exhibit a potential of promoting osteogenic differentiation of MC3T3-E1 cells.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了钛表面形貌对树突状细胞成熟和成骨分化的影响，但与增材制造生物医学方向（如LPBF制造、疲劳测试、多孔结构等）无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), porous structure design, or stress shielding analysis; it focuses solely on in vitro immunomodulation of titanium surfaces.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究不同钛表面处理对树突状细胞成熟的影响及其成骨分化潜力。
summary_zh.method: 将小鼠骨髓树突状细胞接种于PT、SLA和modSLA钛片上，检测成熟标志物和细胞因子。
summary_zh.result: modSLA表面使树突状细胞保持未成熟表型，其条件培养基促进前成骨细胞成骨分化。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞培养实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of titanium surface topography on dendritic cell maturation and its subsequent impact on osteogenic differentiation.
summary_en.method: Murine bone marrow-derived dendritic cells were cultured on titanium disks with PT, SLA, and modSLA surfaces, and maturation markers and cytokine secretion were analyzed.
summary_en.result: The modSLA surface maintained dendritic cells in an immature phenotype, and conditioned medium from these cells promoted osteogenic gene expression in preosteoblasts.
